body.statement:
For every \(a\in\mathcal A_{\rm G}\), use a normalized quasi-uniform spline basis of degree sufficient for \(C^s\) approximation and a growing dimension satisfying
\[
J_n\to\infty,\qquad
\sqrt n\,J_n^{-2s}\to0,\qquad
\frac{J_n^{\alpha_a}}{\sqrt n}\to0,\qquad
\frac{J_n^{\alpha_a+1}\log n}{n}\to0,\qquad
J_n^{-s}\log(n/J_n)\to0,
\]
with \(\alpha_a=0\) under the bounded-support convention.  Then the data-driven clip is asymptotically inactive when the propensity is bounded away from zero and is first-order negligible otherwise under \(\text{ass:finite-variance}\).  The cross-fitted likelihood construction satisfies
\[
\sqrt n\{\widehat q_a(\tau)-q_a(\tau)\}
=n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n{\rm IF}_a(O_i;\tau)+o_P(1)
\]
jointly over \(a\in\mathcal A_{\rm G}\) and \(\tau\in\mathcal T\), with covariance \(E_P[{\rm IF}_a{\rm IF}_{a'}^\top]\).
body.justification: The likelihood Riesz projection produces the learned-propensity score contribution, while Hall tails and the bounded-propensity Hölder branch verify uniform Lindeberg rather than assuming it.
body.gap: Regular QTE theory does not provide this finite-inverse-moment profiled-sieve expansion with the data-driven clipping rule and row-specific uniform Gaussian approximation.
body.consumer: It supplies the regular coordinate and shared cross-arm covariance in mixed and two-Gaussian moving row laws.
body.proof_tex:
We again prove the stronger uniform moving-law expansion.  Fix a finite-variance arm \(a\), write \(q_{a,P}\), \(f_{a,P}\), and \(\mathrm{IF}_{a,P}\) when needed, and let \(L_{a,P}^{\mathrm G}\) be the centered Gaussian vector with covariance
\[
 \Sigma_{a,P}=E_P\!\left[\{\mathrm{IF}_{a,P}(O;\tau)\}_{\tau\in\mathcal T}
 \{\mathrm{IF}_{a,P}(O;\tau)\}_{\tau\in\mathcal T}^{\!\top}\right].
 \tag{G1}
\]
We show both the displayed linearization and
\[
 \sup_{\substack{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm S}:a\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm G}\\
 P\text{ satisfies }\text{ass:gamma-separation}}}
 d_{\mathrm{BL}}\!\left(
 \mathcal L_P[\sqrt n(\widehat q_a-q_{a,P})],
 \mathcal L_P(L_{a,P}^{\mathrm G})\right)\longrightarrow0,
 \tag{G2}
\]
under the stated Gaussian-arm schedules.  The uniform assertion is restricted away from \(\gamma=2\) by \(\text{ass:gamma-separation}\); for each fixed \(P\), the same proof with law-dependent constants establishes the theorem as stated.

For a log-propensity direction \(g\), direct differentiation of the Bernoulli likelihood gives
\[
 s_g(O)=\frac{\{\mathbf1(A=a)-\pi_a(X)\}g(X)}{1-\pi_a(X)},
 \qquad
 \mathcal I_{a,P}(g_1,g_2)=E_P\!\left[
 \frac{\pi_a(X)}{1-\pi_a(X)}g_1(X)g_2(X)\right].
 \tag{G3}
\]
The derivative of the signed functional is
\(\dot\Lambda_{a,P}(g)=E_P\{m_{a,\tau}(X)g(X)\}\).  Its information-space Riesz representer is
\[
 r_{a,\tau,P}(X)=m_{a,\tau}(X)\frac{1-\pi_a(X)}{\pi_a(X)},
 \tag{G4}
\]
because substitution of \(G4\) in \(G3\) gives
\(\mathcal I_{a,P}(r_{a,\tau,P},g)=\dot\Lambda_{a,P}(g)\).  Also
\[
 E_Ps_{r_{a,\tau,P}}^2
 =E_P\!\left[m_{a,\tau}(X)^2\frac{1-\pi_a(X)}{\pi_a(X)}\right]
 \le C_{\mathrm G}
 \tag{G5}
\]
by \(\text{ass:finite-variance}\) and \(|m_{a,\tau}|\le1\).  Thus all divisions and the projection in \(G4\) are legitimate.

Let \(r_{a,\tau,P,J}\) be the information projection of \(G4\) on the likelihood sieve.  On cells at distance \(j/J\) from the endpoint, the boundary link in \(\text{ass:boundary-link}\), the normalized local support of the B-splines, and the Hölder approximation error in \(\text{ass:holder}\) give, after summing the cellwise geometric powers,
\[
 \|s_{r_{a,\tau,P,J}}-s_{r_{a,\tau,P}}\|_{L^2(P)}=o(1),
 \tag{G6}
\]
uniformly for finite \(\gamma_{a,P}>2\), equivalently \(alpha_{a,P}<1\).  The same cell calculation and the likelihood score equation give
\[
 \sqrt n\,|\text{product approximation bias}|\le C\sqrt nJ_n^{-2s},
 \quad
 \sqrt n\,|\text{reciprocal quadratic remainder}|
 =O_P(J_n^{\alpha_{a,P}}/\sqrt n),
 \tag{G7}
\]
and the empirical Hessian replacement is
\(O_P\{J_n^{\alpha_{a,P}+1}\log n/n\}^{1/2}=o_P(1)\).  Each term is \(o_P(1)\) by the displayed tuning conditions.  If \(\gamma_{a,P}=\infty\), the fixed Hölder-ball radius and \(\pi_a=\exp(g_a)\) imply \(\inf_x\pi_a(x)\ge e^{-C}>0\).  Profiling the extra \(\log d_a\) direction against the quasi-uniform spline space gives a residual with squared norm \(O(J_n^{-1})\), a profiled coefficient error \(O_P(\sqrt{J_n/n})\), and maximum sample residual \(O_P\{\log(n/J_n)\}\); the profiled spline-function sup error is
\(O_P\{\sqrt{J_n\log J_n/n}+J_n^{-s}\}\).  Hence \(J_n\log n/n\to0\) and \(J_n^{-s}\log(n/J_n)\to0\) make the fitted propensity uniformly sample-point consistent.  This is the same profiling argument established at the mixed bounded arm in \(\text{prop:finite-variance-sanity}\), with constants uniform over the fixed Hölder ball.

For every fold, \(G3\)--\(G7\), the score equation, and the nonpositive inner product of a concave maximizer's feasible displacement with its normal-cone residual yield
\[
 \sqrt n\sum_{k=1}^K\frac{|I_k|}{n}
 \int m_{a,\tau}(x)
 \frac{\widehat\pi_{a,-k}(x)-\pi_a(x)}{\pi_a(x)}\,dP_X(x)
 =\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=1}^n s_{r_{a,\tau,P}}(O_i)+o_P(1).
 \tag{G8}
\]
The coefficient is one because every observation occurs in \(K-1\) training folds, each of size \(n(K-1)/K+O(1)\).  Conditional on a training fold, cross-fitting makes the centered evaluation error mean zero.  Its conditional variance is bounded by
\[
 C\int\frac{(\widehat\pi_{a,-k}-\pi_a)^2}{\pi_a}\,dP_X
 =O_P(J_n^{-2s}+J_n^{2\alpha_{a,P}}/n)=o_P(1),
 \tag{G9}
\]
where \(2\alpha_{a,P}<\alpha_{a,P}+1\) for finite \(\gamma_{a,P}>2\), and the bounded case uses \(alpha_{a,P}=0\).

Clipping is first-order negligible.  In the bounded case, sample-point consistency and the true common lower bound make it inactive with probability tending to one.  For the following finite-\(\gamma\) comparison only, define the proof intermediate \(b^\circ_{a,P,n}=\vartheta_a/h_{a,P,n}\).  For finite \(\gamma_{a,P}>2\), \(H2\) and Hall integration give
\[
 \sqrt n\left|E_Pm_{a,\tau}(X)
 \left\{\frac{\pi_a(X)}{\pi_a(X)\vee b^\circ_{a,P,n}}-1\right\}\right|
 \le Cn^{1/2-(\gamma_{a,P}-1)/\gamma_{a,P}}=o(1)
 \tag{G10}
\]
uniformly because \(\gamma_{a,P}\ge2+\epsilon_\gamma\).  The centered clipping difference has variance tending uniformly to zero, since
\(E_P[\pi_a(X)^{-1}\mathbf1\{\pi_a(X)\le u\}]\le Cu^{\gamma_{a,P}-2}\), obtained by Stieltjes integration of \(\text{ass:hall}\).  The same count sandwich calculation used in \(H8\), now with the finite-\(\gamma\) Gaussian exponent, shows \(\widehat b_{a,n}/b^\circ_{a,P,n}\to_P1\) when \(\vartheta_a>0\); when \(\vartheta_a=0\), both thresholds are exactly zero.  This transfers \(G10\) to the empirical threshold in both cases.

Knight's identity \(H10\), now with \(v=t/\sqrt n\), \(\text{ass:conditional-density-modulus}\), and \(\text{ass:quantile-density}\) give, uniformly on compact \(t\)-sets,
\[
 \widehat Q^{\mathrm G}_{a,n,\tau}(t)
 =\frac12f_{a,P}(\tau)t^2-
 t\,\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=1}^n
 \left[\frac{\mathbf1(A_i=a)\psi_{a,\tau}(Y_i)}{\pi_a(X_i)}
 -s_{r_{a,\tau,P}}(O_i)\right]+o_P(1).
 \tag{G11}
\]
Using \(G4\), the bracket in \(G11\) is exactly
\[
 m_{a,\tau}(X_i)+\frac{\mathbf1(A_i=a)
 \{\psi_{a,\tau}(Y_i)-m_{a,\tau}(X_i)\}}{\pi_a(X_i)}
 =f_{a,P}(\tau)\mathrm{IF}_{a,P}(O_i;\tau).
 \tag{G12}
\]
It is centered because \(E_P\psi_{a,\tau}\{Y(a)\}=0\).

We finally verify the uniform Gaussian approximation rather than assume it.  Since \(\mathcal T\) is finite, \(G12\), the density lower bound, and \(|m|,|\psi|\le1\) reduce multivariate Lindeberg to the inverse-weight term.  For finite \(\gamma_{a,P}\ge2+\epsilon_\gamma\), Stieltjes integration of the uniform Hall bound gives, for large \(x\),
\[
 E_P\!\left[\frac{\mathbf1(A=a)}{\pi_a(X)^2}
 \mathbf1\{\pi_a(X)^{-1}>x\}\right]
 =E_P\!\left[\frac1{\pi_a(X)}\mathbf1\{\pi_a(X)<x^{-1}\}\right]
 \le Cx^{-(\gamma_{a,P}-2)}\le Cx^{-\epsilon_\gamma}.
 \tag{G13}
\]
For \(\gamma_{a,P}=\infty\), the common Hölder-ball lower bound \(\pi_a\ge e^{-C}\) makes the summands uniformly bounded.  Taking \(x\) proportional to \(\sqrt n\) in \(G13\) proves uniform Lindeberg.  For every fixed coefficient vector, expand the characteristic function of the corresponding scalar linear projection at order two on the Lindeberg-truncated event and bound the remainder by its truncated second moment.  The resulting formula is the characteristic function of the centered Gaussian vector having the row covariance \(G1\); Fourier inversion after Gaussian smoothing, followed by removal of the smoothing, gives uniform bounded-Lipschitz convergence.  No covariance convergence across rows is needed.  The lower curvature bound then maps \(G11\) to its smallest convex minimizer and yields
\[
 \sqrt n\{\widehat q_a(\tau)-q_{a,P}(\tau)\}
 =\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=1}^n\mathrm{IF}_{a,P}(O_i;\tau)+o_P(1)
 \tag{G14}
\]
jointly over the finite arm--quantile vector, with a remainder uniform in \(P\).  Equations \(G13\)--\(G14\) prove \(G2\) and the asserted covariance formula.
